unresolved_added: The printed horizon rule is distance=sqrt(1.5 h); it differs from the commonly cited coefficient-times-square-root form and gives about 7.75 miles at 40 feet rather than the later 9-mile value.
The paper redefines 1,000 simultaneous users as 1,000 possible requesters with a parameterized average rate, materially weakening the original concurrency interpretation.
CTCSS or a privacy tone gates repeater activation but does not by itself prevent two simultaneous radio signals from physically interfering.
The claimed one-to-two-second delay is not attributable to radio-wave propagation across an 80-mile domain; equipment and protocol delay are not separately modeled.
Downlink and handheld uplink ranges are asymmetric, yet coverage and communication feasibility are treated largely through circular reach without a complete link-budget rule.
The model deliberately queues conflicting requests instead of counting them as failed, so interference is less heavily penalized than the paper's own service definition suggests.
A 600 kHz duplex offset is treated as a minimum distinguishable channel spacing without a spectrum plan, occupied bandwidth, adjacent-channel, or regulatory analysis.
The assumption that users listen on all privacy lines for several minutes before every request is operationally implausible and leaves an unresolved CITE placeholder.
Q omits waiting time, fairness, transmission duration, hop count, repeated retries, and the distribution of service across users.
Algorithm 1 is order-dependent because it greedily scans the queue; no randomization, priority policy, fairness diagnostic, or maximum waiting time is defined.
The interference predicate used by Algorithm 1 is not formalized, so the simulation cannot be reproduced from the pseudocode alone.

The request-distance expression is called Poisson but contains a binomial coefficient, an undefined k, l factorial, and a binomial-like final term; it is neither a standard Poisson PMF nor a fully defined alternative.
The claimed lower bound is only a lower bound within networks generated by this heuristic and does not establish a global minimum repeater count.
The printed population field has a positive quadratic exponent and no negative one-half factor, so it is not a normalizable bivariate Gaussian density.
The paper does not explain how Gaussian samples outside the radius-40 circle are rejected, truncated, wrapped, or resampled.
Figure 1 compares synthetic coordinate plots with an actual density image using different color systems, scales, and no common units, so the claimed similarity is qualitative.
Five staggered 600 kHz pairs across 145-148 MHz use band-edge values but do not document occupied bandwidth, repeater coordination, or whether all pairings are legally deployable.
The weak E-prime extension, simultaneous-shutdown rule, and timeout behavior have no power threshold, delay model, stability proof, or simulation.
The privacy-line routing example assumes effectively instantaneous duplicate forwarding and postpones the resulting offset-signal collision to the limitations section.
Line 54 is used as a stop signal without a complete allocation and reuse rule across the whole network.
Algorithm 2 alternates MaximumRepeaterRange, MaximumRegionRange, RepeaterRanges, and UserRanges, leaving its input-output interface inconsistent.
K-means minimizes within-cluster squared distance, not uncovered users, repeater count, interference, or network capacity, so centroid placement is only a heuristic for the stated objective.
A minimum-total-distance spanning plan over components does not necessarily minimize the number of added repeaters when ranges and required integer connectors matter.
Algorithm 3 does not define the ceiling rule for numRepeatersRequired and its repeated closest-component procedure is asserted to be an MST without a complete proof.
Algorithm 4 does not reconcile graph depths beyond channel 5 with the extended-chain construction and does not verify channel compatibility on cycles or multi-parent layers.
The five generated populations per population type are too few for stable uncertainty estimates, and no random seeds or reproducible code are supplied.
The statement that more initial clusters increase capacity is not generally monotone: several 5-clump and 10-clump table entries decline as clusters increase.
The claim that even the 5-clump standard deviation is below 1.5 percent conflicts with displayed values such as 0.102 and 0.074 if table entries are proportions.
Table 4 is captioned as a percentage but reports fractions between zero and one, inviting a factor-100 interpretation error.
The recursive subnetwork feature is explicitly unfinished and unevaluated, and the text points to Figure 4 although the comparison is Figure 5.
The mountainous-terrain extension gives no propagation model, elevation data interface, asymmetric distance definition, objective function, annealing schedule, or experiment.
The conclusion's 15-cluster claim of over 97 percent coverage and about 95 percent transmission is not uniform across population types; the 5-clump capacity entry is only 0.830.
The claimed maximum of roughly 25 distinct locations and the typical network of about 40 repeaters require a co-location accounting rule that is not explicitly reconciled.
The privacy-line count leading to the 25-location cap is not derived in a complete allocation table, and duplicate processing delays are not quantified.
The greedy repeater-removal proposal depends on an undefined network-quality loss and has no optimality, complexity, or connectivity guarantee.
